TOP OF BOOK

  • MACRO — Hormuz Re-Escalation / Oil [NEW] — US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz reinstated effective 16:00 ET 14 July; Trump announces 20% cargo fee on all transiting ships; Iran declares passage "currently unfeasible."
    • Vs. baseline: The June ceasefire had temporarily de-escalated the disruption and allowed limited Hormuz traffic recovery. Maritime traffic that had ticked up following the US-Iran MoU has now declined sharply amid renewed fighting. The US reinstatement of the blockade is the proximate cause of renewed closure. Brent futures jumped 9.5% to above $83/bbl on Monday, WTI topped $78 — Brent is on track for its biggest single-day gain since May 2020. WTI rose a further 1.83% to $79.57 on Tuesday; Brent climbed 1.7% to $84.72, extending Monday's 9.6% surge.
    • Read: ECB June hike was premised on the war generating inflation pressures; the June baseline already projected headline inflation at 3.0% in 2026. Hormuz re-closure re-opens the severe scenario: energy cost re-acceleration, widening core passthrough, and pressure for a further September hike. Citi warned that Trump's Hormuz toll "materially raises the risk of further military escalation" and that the prospect of Iran walking away from the MoU "would most likely see higher for longer oil prices." Transmission to EU financials: (a) NII: September hike probability spikes → short-end re-pricing bullish for bank NII; (b) Provisions: energy-exposed corporates, shipping/trade credit books face stress; (c) Funding: risk-off spread widening, particularly AT1 and SNP in peripheral names; (d) ECB TPI may be needed if sovereign spreads widen on growth fears. Leg: bank equities mixed (NII+ vs. provisions—); AT1/SNP spreads widen; senior HY energy-exposed credits under pressure. Action: MONITOR / reduce duration on European bank credit; fade any spread compression in energy-sector CLO tranches.
    • Sources: CNBC, Yahoo Finance, Al Jazeera
  • US BANK EARNINGS / June CPI — Binary pair lands today [IN LINE] — Q2 2026 earnings from JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo all land Tuesday alongside the June CPI report. Results not yet confirmed as of press time; read-through to European banks is the key.
    • Vs. baseline: Options markets priced in elevated volatility — implied moves ranging from 4.4% for JPMorgan to 6.0% for Goldman Sachs. Consensus expected: JPMorgan EPS ~$5.80 on revenue of ~$51.3bn; Finance sector Q2 earnings expected +12.6% YoY on +8.4% revenues. For June CPI: consensus is headline CPI -0.1% MoM; annual rate falls from 4.2% to ~3.9%, driven by a 10% June gasoline price decline — but core CPI expected at ~2.9% YoY, above target. The Fed raised its 2026 inflation forecast to 3.6% at the June FOMC and shifted the dot-plot to 3.8%, signaling higher for longer.
    • Read: The CPI soft-headline / sticky-core combination is the trap: a negative MoM print will generate "cooling inflation" headlines, but a one-month dip in energy prices does not reflect a change in the macro trajectory — and with Hormuz re-blockaded from today, the July CPI print will re-accelerate sharply. Watch NII guidance and provision builds from JPM/BAC/WFC as the leading indicator for European bank credit quality. A beat on IB/trading at GS is directionally positive for BNP/SocGen FICC revenues. Any reserve build on energy/trade credit would be a precursor signal for European syndicated books. Leg: equity positive if NII stable and provisions contained; AT1 spreads may widen on Hormuz risk-off bid regardless of print. Action: DIG IN as results emerge; key watch = JPM provision and NII guidance vs. current sell-side models.
    • Sources: IG Bank, Kiplinger CPI preview, BLS (June CPI release scheduled 08:30 ET today)

BY NAME / THEME

  • UniCredit (UCG IM) / Commerzbank (CBK GR) [DELTA ▲] — ECB control-ruling clock running; UCG at 49.65% voting rights; ECB decision expected by September 2026.
    • Vs. baseline: UniCredit is set to control almost 48% of Commerzbank's shares; taking into account treasury shares, the Italian firm will have 49.65% of votes once physical transfer completes. Independent shareholder take-up was less than 2% — Commerzbank described this as "clear evidence that the offer lacked appeal." The critical gate is now regulatory: all eyes are on the ECB, which must rule on whether UniCredit may raise its stake beyond the 30% and 45% thresholds — a decision expected by September 2026.
    • Read: The capital trap is the key risk for UCG equity: a 49.7% voting stake is likely to prompt the ECB to rule UniCredit has control of Commerzbank; being declared in control without majority ownership would force UCG to consolidate a minority stake, a major blow to capital reserves due to minority accounting rules. Orcel acknowledged merging accounts with Commerzbank without majority ownership would cost UniCredit 40% more in terms of core capital. UCG equity: short-term neutral (deal optionality priced), medium-term CET1 drag risk if ECB control ruling lands before majority secured. CBK equity: Commerzbank standalone case supported by Momentum 2030 strategy targeting net profit ≥€3.4bn for 2026, rising to €5.9bn long-term with 21% ROE; ECB hiking cycle would bolster NII and support high payout ratio. Also: UCG could amend swap contracts currently cash-only, handing it a further 11.5% of Commerzbank, which is the next potential escalation lever. Action: MONITOR UCG CET1 sensitivity to ECB control ruling; CBK standalone remains a carry + corporate action option story at current levels ahead of Q2 print (6 Aug).
    • Sources: Bloomberg, Axios, Commerzbank IR, Business Recorder / Reuters
  • ECB — Schnabel Speech (13 Jul), Cipollone Interview (13 Jul) [IN LINE] — Both in-line with the post-June-hike hawkish-hold message; no new rate signal, no deviation from June policy statement.
    • Vs. baseline: Schnabel spoke in Münster on 13 July on "How to foster growth and resilience in Europe." The speech addressed European competitiveness and fiscal dynamics rather than near-term rate signalling. Cipollone's Jornal de Negocios interview was focused on the digital euro legislative process: the ECB aims to be ready for first issuance in 2029, assuming the legislative process is completed by end of 2026, with a pilot phase to launch in 2027. Simulations applied holding limits of €500–€3,000; within these limits no relevant risks to financial stability were identified.
    • Read: No rate repricing signal from either speaker — consistent with the June GC stance of data-dependence and market pricing of a September follow-on hike. Digital euro comments confirm no near-term threat to bank deposit franchises at the ceiling sizes modelled; deposit funding costs and NII projections for euro area banks are unaffected at current modelled limits. The Hormuz re-escalation (above) is the event that will force the next signal from Lagarde/Schnabel. The relevant framing remains the June GC minutes: ongoing disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz had reinforced expectations that oil prices would remain higher for longer. Action: NO ACTION on these speeches; monitor for emergency GC communication if Brent >$90.
    • Sources: ECB Schnabel speech (13 Jul), ECB Cipollone interview (13 Jul)
  • European Banks — H1 2026 Earnings Season Opens Today [IN LINE] — European bank earnings season set to kick off today, 14 July 2026. No European bank prints confirmed pre-open; season runs through late July/early August.
    • Vs. baseline: Q1 2026 set a strong bar: Q1 results came in stronger than expected; BBVA +8% net profit, HSBC +12%, Barclays +16%, UniCredit +16% YoY, Commerzbank +9%. Sector consensus for 2026 has been trimmed: 2026 profit growth forecast revised to 9%, down from pre-conflict estimate of 10%, reflecting Hormuz energy shock impact. Key risk to watch: higher expected credit losses and provisions, increased energy-related operating costs, offset by trading revenues and NIM resilience in a rising-rate environment.
    • Read: The Hormuz re-escalation injects a read-through risk for Q2 management commentary on: (a) energy-sector and trade-finance exposures in credit books; (b) NII guidance — September hike now more probable, positive for NII trajectories; (c) provisions guidance — any pre-emptive reserve build for commodity/energy book. Also watch: Barclays on M&A pipeline; Barclays projected to have an M&A war chest of roughly £3.6bn following the Evelyn Partners loss to NatWest. HSBC: cited significant credit impairments linked to the Iran war at Q1 — Q2 print will be pivotal for HSBC equity given ongoing conflict. Action: MONITOR; DIG IN on HSBC and Barclays when H1 releases drop; build watch for any name guiding down provisions.
    • Sources: Rabobank earnings calendar, Euronews (Q1 context)
  • ECB Rate Path — September Hike Probability Rising [DELTA ▲] — Hormuz re-blockade re-prices the ECB's September decision toward another 25bp hike; market had been wavering on whether the ceasefire-period moderation would prompt a pause.
    • Vs. baseline: Post-June hike, the ECB press conference stated: headline inflation expected at 3.0% in 2026, 2.3% in 2027; core at 2.5% for 2026–27. The June minutes showed markets pricing in ~three 25bp hikes overall, with one in June and another fully priced for September. The Hormuz re-closure removes the ceasefire scenario from the ECB's "favourable" illustrative path. Growth revised to 0.8% in 2026, with downside risks from the war's impact on commodity markets and confidence.
    • Read: Higher-for-longer oil means headline inflation in July/August data re-accelerates (the June soft print is a one-month energy artefact). Core stickiness at ~2.9% combined with a renewed energy shock locks in September hike and raises odds of a third move. Transmission to financials book: (a) NII bullish for deposit-rich banks with asset sensitivity; (b) funding costs for AT1/SNP issuers rise at the margin; (c) sovereign-bank nexus: higher rates raise peripheral sovereign carry risk if growth slows further — watch OAT-Bund and BTP-Bund spreads; (d) mortgage book quality: variable-rate markets (Italy, Spain, Portugal) face continued borrower stress. Action: MONITOR; long Commerzbank/Spanish bank NII sensitivity vs. short peripheral SNP spread risk.
    • Sources: ECB June meeting minutes (9 Jul), ECB June press conference
  • Payments / Fintech — No Immediate Catalyst; Sector in Background [IN LINE] — No fresh Adyen, Worldline, or Nexi news in last 24h. Adyen H1 results expected in August; Worldline turnaround ongoing.
    • Vs. baseline: Last known: Adyen H1 revenues grew 20%, EBITDA margins above 50%, but stock fell 18% after management reduced H2 guidance citing Trump tariff impact on Asia-Pacific clients. Worldline remains in turnaround mode. The Cipollone digital euro interview is moderately relevant: ECB targeting 2029 issuance removes near-term franchise threat to payment processors.
    • Read: The Hormuz/oil shock creates an indirect macro drag on consumer spending volumes — negative for payment processor take rates and transaction fee revenues in energy-sensitive markets; FX volatility from oil repricing also raises hedging costs for cross-border payment flows. Watch Adyen H1 for any updated tariff/APAC guidance. Action: MONITOR; no action today.
    • Sources: Business of Payments, ECB Cipollone interview

CREDIT CORNER

  • AT1 / European Bank Credit — Hormuz Risk-Off [NEW] — Brent +9.5% yesterday; oil re-escalation is a direct spread-widening catalyst for European bank AT1 and SNP.
    • Read: Euro area banks resilient per ECB assessment, but a sudden sharp drop in asset prices potentially amplified by the non-bank financial sector, and deteriorating asset quality particularly in energy and trade-sensitive sectors, would pose risks to financial stability. The risk-off bid from Hormuz should widen AT1 spreads across the board but hit periphery harder (BBVA, Santander, UniCredit AT1s most exposed). The ECB hiking cycle simultaneously supports call economics on AT1 paper — watch for any issuer that had a borderline extension-risk call coming up. BoE Governor Bailey's June Sintra warning is also live: "leverage in equity markets — hedge fund leverage, ETF leverage — those things are changing"; "if you look at private credit, the question we're asking is, are those the things that actually can move from tail risk into a broader consequence?" Action: MONITOR AT1 spread levels on open; hedge peripheral AT1 longs via CDS if spreads widen >20bp intraday.
    • Sources: ECB June statement, CNBC ECB Forum (Bailey Sintra remarks)

CALENDAR AHEAD

  • TODAY (14 Jul): US June CPI, BLS, 08:30 ET — consensus headline -0.1% MoM / ~3.9% YoY; core ~2.9% YoY. Soft headline expected (energy base); core is the read. JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Citigroup all reporting Q2 before open. US blockade of Strait of Hormuz enters force at 16:00 ET per CENTCOM. Watch for European equity open pricing in weekend escalation.
  • Wed 15 Jul: ASML reports Q2 before open. Morgan Stanley, BlackRock, BNY Mellon, PNC Q2 earnings. ASML order intake is a real-economy signal for European tech-sector credit and capex sentiment.
  • Thu 16 Jul: UnitedHealth, GE Aerospace, ABB, Abbott, US Bancorp, State Street Q2. ABB is a European industrial proxy; State Street / BNY are asset-manager read-throughs for AuM and custody fees. TSMC earnings — semiconductor demand gauge with read into DZ Bank / BNP tech lending books.
  • W/C 21 Jul: ECB Governing Council meeting (24 Jul). No rate change expected at this meeting (next live meeting for hike is September); but press conference language on Hormuz escalation and August inflation path will be critical for September pricing. An in-line hold with a hawkish statement is the base case — a miss toward dovish language would be the surprise.
  • 6 Aug: Commerzbank Q2 2026 results. Key event in the UCG/CBK saga — Commerzbank standalone earnings and any management commentary on the UniCredit situation will be closely watched.
